In addition to the matrix BCC Nb phase, three different Nb5Si3-type silicides, a-Nb5Si3 (tetragonal, D8l), b-Nb5Si3 (tetragonal, D8m), and c-Nb5Si3 (hexagonal, D88), are identified.
In addition to the matrix BCC Nb phase, three different Nb5Si3-type silicides, a-Nb5Si3 (tetragonal, D8l), b-Nb5Si3 (tetragonal, D8m), and c-Nb5Si3 (hexagonal, D88), are identified.
The primary Nb5Si3-type is detected as b-Nb5Si3 in Ta-B, whereas it is a-Nb5Si3 in all other alloys.
c-Nb5Si3 is only detected in Zr-B, Ta-A, and Al-B alloys.
In addition, a Nb3Si-type silicide with a tetragonal structure is also detected in all alloys.

attributes.morphology: large proeutectic islands in dendritic form

evidence.quote: In Group A alloys (Zr-A, Ta-A, Al-A), ssNb appears as large proeutectic islands in dendritic form.
ssNb is also observed in the fine eutectic colonies along with Nb5Si3 and Nb3Si phases. Interlamellar spacing is 200–500 nm in Zr-A, 200–600 nm in Ta-A, and 500–800 nm in Al-B.
Interlamellar spacing is 200–500 nm in Zr-A, 200–600 nm in Ta-A, and 500–800 nm in Al-B.
Interlamellar spacing is 200–500 nm in Zr-A, 200–600 nm in Ta-A, and 500–800 nm in Al-B.
The eutectic mixture of ssNb, (a,c)-Nb5Si3, and Nb3Si is detected in fine lamella areas in all Group A alloys.
In Zr-B, ssNb appears as islands of various sizes, from nano-scale to over 10 lm. a-Nb5Si3 is observed as primary silicide islands.

Ta was selected due to its high solubility limit to Nb, thereby expected to be effective in increasing the solid solution strengthening effect of the Nb-based matrix.
Furthermore, Zr-A exhibited a serration in stress–strain curves, known as Portevin–Le Chatelier (PLC) effect. This occurs due to the interaction between solutes and mobile dislocations.

Zr-B and Ta-A exhibit softening behavior after reaching peak stress, while it is absent in Zr-A and Al-A, which might be triggered by continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) in ssNb and silicide phases, activated by external applied stress and high-temperature environment.
Zr-B exhibits large primary a-Nb5Si3 islands. They are considered to be effective obstacles for mobile dislocations traveling through the ssNb phase.
